messages:
maya: Noticed repeated APAC GPU contention 01:00-04:00 local nights for the last 4 days. Patterns: marketing promo + a customer autotest running long-sequence evals.
liam: Did the autoscaler open extra nodes or hit any quotas?
maya: It opened burst nodes. We exceeded region burst_budget and hit per-tenant soft_quota, then a peering jitter between apac and global control plane caused node readiness flaps.
olga: Got logs?
maya: Pasted the scaler event tail:
```
2026-03-14T23:05:11Z scale up: pool apac-gpu +8 (burst)
2026-03-14T23:12:02Z node-not-ready -> Reconcile -> cordon 4 nodes
2026-03-14T23:12:45Z burst_budget: tenant=acct-123 consumed=85% holdback=15%
```
liam: Network-induced kubelet timeouts -> pod Terminating cascade. That's what caused the rapid evictions.
ryan_product: From product: promo doubled short-chat QPS but also one integration started indexing long documents. We expected short spikes, not tens of minutes sustained.
olga: Proposal: split autoscaler logic into two budgets: transient token-bucket for very short bursts (<=3min) and a sustained GPU-minute budget sampled over rolling 30min windows.
maya: Current moving-average smoothing collapses short bursts into perceived sustained demand. We need separate signals.
liam: Implementation consideration: token-bucket per-tenant requires persistent counters and cross-controller coordination. Simpler: maintain two metric streams - short_window (exp decay 60-180s) and long_window (15-60min) and apply thresholds differently.
olga: Draft policy config (canary):
```
short_burst:
  window_seconds: 180
  bucket_capacity_gpu_seconds: 1800
  ephemeral_node_cap_pct: 8
sustained_budget:
  window_seconds: 1800
  threshold_gpu_seconds: 900
holdback:
  sustained_to_reserved: true
  reserve_multiplier: 1.1
drain_safety:
  block_aggressive_downscale_if_pod_terminating_pct_gt: 10
  window_seconds: 120
```
maya: Also add downscale safety: if control-plane sees increased apac-controlplane-latency or >10% pods in Terminating for 60-120s, delay scale-downs and extend node grace to avoid churn.
liam: Agree. We saw ~35% pods stuck Terminating during the last jitter. That triggered eviction storms.
olga: Cost tradeoff: ephemeral on-demand nodes in APAC cost ~30% more vs reserved but prevent retry storms. Consider preemptible mix for ephemeral if provisioning time is acceptable.
ryan_product: Product side: we can pre-authorize transient reserve for specific promo windows for top-tier customers to reduce blast radius.
maya: Canary plan:
- Night 0: deploy short_burst telemetry only (no enforcement).
- Night 1: enable ephemeral_node_cap and drain_safety with ephemeral cap=5% of pool.
- Night 2: enable sustained_budget enforcement and reserve_multiplier.
- Week A/B: 10% of pools run baseline, 90% run new policy. Measure.
liam: Metrics to capture: ephemeral_node_count, sustained_reserved_nodes, node_eviction_rate, pod_terminating_pct, p95_latency_by_region, gpu_hours_by_tenant, failed_request_rate.
olga: Runbook notes for canary:
- Rollback command:
  kubectl -n infra set configmap autoscaler-policy --from-file=policy=./prod-policy.yaml && kubectl rollout restart deploy/autoscaler -n infra
- Observe node_evictions > baseline -> rollback immediately.
- If apac-controlplane-latency > 500ms for >2min -> pause canary.

maya: I'll schedule the telemetry-only deploy tonight, then enable enforcement the next low-traffic night. Will attach synthetic load that simulates promo + long-seq clients.
liam: Add a tagging flag to ephemeral nodes so we can separate cost and uptime metrics: node.label=burst_ephemeral=true
ryan_product: I'll coordinate with marketing and notify dev customers to avoid heavy indexing during canary window.
olga: Also file a small spike-resilience ticket to test spot boot times + KV cache warmup; if preemptible is used we need warm-cache priming strategy.
maya: Deploy-bot: rolling canary: autoscaler-controller v3.2.2-canary scheduled at 2026-03-16T00:50:00Z
deploy-bot: Deployment succeeded: autoscaler-controller v3.2.2-canary at 2026-03-16T00:52:33Z
maya: (update) telemetry-only night complete. Short-window spikes absorbed, no flaps. Enabling ephemeral enforcement tonight.
liam: Nice. Keep watch on pod_terminating_pct and apac-provisioning-latency.
maya: Will post morning charts and a final recommendation. Thanks all :thumbsup:
